annotations.title: Searching the ſcriptures.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> The Heretikes vſe this place to proue that the hearers muſt trie and iudge by the Scriptures, whether their teachers and preachers doctrine be true, and ſo reiect that that they find not in the Scriptures. as though here the ſheepe vvere made iudges of their Paſtors, the people of the Prieſts, and men and women of al ſortes, euen of S. Paules doctrine it ſelf: Which were the moſt foliſh diſorder in the world. And they did not therfore read the Scriptures of the old Teſtament (for none of the nevv vvere yet extant commonly) to diſpute vvith the Apoſtle, or to trie and iudge of his doctrine, or vvhether they ſhould beleeue him or no: for they were bound to beleeue him and obey his word, vvhether he alleaged Scripture or no, and whether they could reade or vnderſtand the Scriptures or no. but it was a great comfort and confirmation for the Ievves that had the Scriptures, to finde euen as S. Paul ſaid, that Chriſt vvas God, crucified, riſen, and aſcended to heauen: which by his preaching and expounding they vnderſtood, and neuer before, though they read them, and heard them read euery Sabboth. <mn>[2]</mn> As it is a great comfort to a Catholike man, to heare the Scriptures declared & alleaged moſt euidently for the Churches truth againſt Heretikes, in Sermons or othervviſe. And it doth the Catholikes good & much confirmeth them, to vew diligently the places alleaged by the Catholike preachers. Yet they muſt not be iudges for al that, ouer their owne Paſtors, whom Chriſt commaundeth them to heare and obey, and by vvhom they heare the true ſenſe of Scriptures.

notes.text: The people may not iudge of the sense of Scriptures.
The comfort of Christian men by hearing or reading the Scriptures.

annotations.title: Superſtitious.
annotations.text: [1] S. Paul calleth not them ſuperſtitious for adoring the true and only God with much deuotion or many ceremonies or in comely preſcribed order, or for doing due reuerence to holy Sacraments, to Saincts and their memories, Images, or Monuments: or for keeping the preſcribed lavves, daies, and faſtes of the Church, or for fulfilling vowes made to God, or for bleſſing vvith the ſigne of the Croſſe, or for capping and kneeling at the name of IESVS, or for religiouſly vſing creatures ſanctified in the ſame name, or any other Chriſtian obſeruation, for which our new Maiſters condemne the Catholike people of Superſtition: them ſelues wholy voide of that vice by al vviſe mens iudgement, becauſe they haue in maner taken avvay al religion, and are become Epicureians and Atheiſts: vvho are neuer troubled with ſuperſtition, becauſe it is a vice conſiſting in exceſſe of vvorſhip or religion, whereof they are void. [2] but the Apoſtle calleth them ſuperſtitious for worſhipping the Idols and goddes of the Heathen, and [3] for the feare that they had, leſt they ſhould leaue out any God that vvas vnknowen to them: for thus their Altar was inſcribed: Dijs Aſiæ, Europa, & Lybiæ, Deo ignoto & peregrino. that is, To the gods of Aſia, Europe, and Lybia: to the vnknowen and ſtrange God. This ſuperſtition (ſaith S. Auguſtine) [4] is wholy taken avvay from the Church by Chriſts incarnation, and by the Apoſtles preaching, and by Martyrs holy life and death. [5] Neither doth the Catholike Church allow this or any other kinde of ſuperſtitious obſeruation. Only we muſt take heede that we beleeue not her Aduerſaries definition of ſuperſtition, for they vvould imply therein al true religion.

notes.text: The Apostle speaketh of the Heathens superstition.
δεισιδαίμονας. Aug. de cons. Euang. li. 1 c. 26.
The Catholic Church alloweth no superstition.

annotations.title: The Diuinitie to be like.
annotations.text: Nothing can be made by mans hand of vvhat forme or ſort ſo euer, that is like to Gods eſſence, or to the forme or ſhape of his Godhead or Diuinitie. therfore howſoeuer the Heathens did paint or graue their Idols, they vvere nothing like to God. And this alſo is impertinently alleaged by Heretikes againſt the Churches images: Which are not made, either to be adored with godly honour, or to be any reſemblance of the Diuinitie or any of the three perſons in Godhead, but only of Chriſt as he was in forme of man, who in that reſpect may be truely expreſſed, as other men by their purtraites: and of the Holy Ghoſt, not as he is in him ſelf, but as he appeared in firy tongues or in the ſimilitude of a dooue, or ſuch like. [1] And ſo to paint or graue any of the three perſons as they appeared viſibly and corporally, is no more inconuenient or vnlawful, then it vvas vndecent for them to appeare in ſuch formes. And therfore to paint or portraite the Father alſo being the firſt perſon, as he hath ſhevved him ſelf in viſion to any of the Prophetes of the old or new Teſtament (namely to Daniel as an old man) [2] or the three Angels repreſenting the three Perſons to Abraham, [3]or the one Angel that wraſtling vvith Iacob bare our Lords Perſon, [4]no ſuch thing is any vvhere forbidden, but is very agreable to the peoples inſtruction. In vvhich ſort the Angels vvere commonly pourtered [5] (and namely the Cherubins ouer the Propitiatorie) as they be novv in the Church, not in their natural forme, but vvith corporal vvinges (as the Seraphins appeared to Eſay the Prophete) [6] to expreſſe their qualitie and office of being Gods Angels, that is, Meſſengers: and God the Father with the world in his hand, to ſignifie his creation and gouernement of the ſame, and ſuch like: Whereof the people being vvel inſtructed may take much good, and no harme in the world, being now through their faith in Chriſt far from al fond imagination of the falſe gods of the Pagans. [7] And therfore S. Gregorie [8] ſaith of the Churches Images, That which ſcripture or writing doth to the readers, the ſame doth the picture to the ſimple that looke therevpon. for in it euen the ignorant ſee vvhat they ought to folovv, in it they do read, that knovv no letters. Where he calleth it a matter of antiquitie and very conuenient, that in holy places Images were painted to the peoples inſtruction, ſo they be taught that they may not be adored with diuine honour. and he in the ſame place ſharply rebuketh Serenus the Biſhop of Maſſilia, that of indiſcrete zele he vvould take avvay Images, rather then teach the people how to vſe them.

notes.text: How there may be Images or resemblances of the thre persons in Trinitie, and of Angels.
Images are for the people's instruction.

annotations.title: Dionyſius Areopagita.
annotations.text: ◦ This is that famous Denys that firſt conuerted France, and wrote thoſe notable and diuine vvorkes de Eccleſiaſtica & cæleſti hierarchia, de diuinis nominibus, and others, in vvhich he confirmeth and proueth plainely almoſt al things that the Church now vſeth in the miniſtration of the holy Sacraments, and affirmeth that he learned them of the Apoſtles, giuing alſo teſtimonie for the Catholike faith in moſt things now controuerſed, ſo plainely, that our Aduerſaries haue no ſhift but to deny this Denys to haue been the author of them, feyning that they be an others of later age. Vvhich is an old flight of Heretikes, but moſt proper to theſe of al others. Who ſeeing al antiquitie againſt them, are forced to be more bold or rather impudent then others in that point.

notes.text: S. Dionysius Areopagita is al for the Catholikes.
